cue: The view is wide and blurry, and it runs slowly, then jumps ahead.
rows: Most insects see less than a sixtieth as much detail as people do.
Flies and dragonflies can see a light flicker more than 100 times a second, and one beetle up to 400. People stop at about 60. This view runs slowly and then jumps ahead to suggest the difference.
Bees and some other insects can see ultraviolet light, which people can’t. Phone cameras capture very little of it, so the violet tint in this view stands in for it.
